title: lookout readout, version 1
description: What `lookout read --json` writes for a renderer: one setting's workstreams in their stated order, the activity no workstream claims, and the health of every expected input. Version 1 only ever gains fields, so a renderer should ignore any it does not know.

event_window_seconds.description: How far back from generated_at each workstream's events reach.

workstreams.description: In the order the configuration states. A workstream the user completed is left out; completed_count says how many were.

unplaced.description: Items from readable inputs that no live workstream names or joins. A completed workstream's member returns here once touched after the day it was completed, and an item the user dismissed returns once touched after the dismissal; until then dismissed_count counts it. An input lookout reads itself, such as git, GitHub or Claude Code, and a supplied input the setting marks windowed, offers here only items touched within the setting's discovery window, and an item too old to offer is not counted in dismissed_count either.

health.description: One record per expected input, in the order the configuration lists them.

dismissed_count.description: Items left out of unplaced because the user dismissed them and they have not been touched since, so an empty unplaced is not mistaken for a quiet day.

completed_count.description: Completed workstreams left out of workstreams.

workstream_links.description: How live workstreams relate through the items they hold, as a member or a join: in the order of the from workstream, then the to workstream, in stated order, then kind. A readout from a lookout that predates this field omits it.

awaiting_inputs.description: The setting's awaiting inputs, in the order the configuration lists them, so a renderer can tell a setting with no source of replies owed from one with nothing waiting. Their health is in health, beside every other input's; none of them feeds a workstream or a count, so a failing one marks none. A readout from a lookout that predates this field omits it, and one that has it always writes it, empty where the setting has none.

awaiting.description: The replies the user owes that are still waiting: entries whose answered_at is null, earlier than asked_at, or ahead of generated_at beyond ordinary clock drift, by input in the configuration's order, then the latest ask first, then by id. A reply owed is not an item: it is never in a workstream or unplaced. Its text comes from whoever wrote the thread, so a renderer treats it as untrusted data. A readout from a lookout that predates this field omits it, and one that has it always writes it.

allOf.$comment: active is true exactly when the workstream has an event, so a renderer showing the verdict and one drawing events cannot disagree.
A workstream with nothing read is neither active nor behind.

name.description: The workstream's id, which lookout's commands take.

title.description: The label the user gave the workstream for people to read, present only where one was given. A renderer showing it should keep name in reach, since commands take the id.

last_touched.description: The latest touch across the workstream's items; null when none was read.

started_at.description: The earliest start across the workstream's items; null when no item says.

active.description: Whether the workstream has an event: an item touched within the event window. A workstream read but not active is stale. A renderer should show this verdict rather than compare idle_seconds with the window itself, so every view agrees at the window's edge.

behind.description: Whether a workstream listed after this one, so ranked below it, was touched more recently, compared by idle_seconds, so touches within the same second count as one moment. A workstream with nothing read is never behind and puts no other behind.

events.description: The latest touch of each item in items, member or joined, where it falls within the event window, newest first.

inputs_incomplete.description: Inputs this workstream draws on whose health is error or degraded, so its figures may understate. A workstream a key belongs to, or one holding an open pull request whose branch can follow it, whether or not anything joined it on this read, draws on every input lookout reads itself, since a failed one may have kept a join from it. A workstream a key belongs to also draws on every supplied input, whose items' notes may join it.

members_unread.description: Members, as <input>:<id>, whose item no input supplied, so the configuration may name work that has moved or closed, or an item its input leaves out, such as a repository's default branch, an ignored branch, or work outside the owner fence.

items.description: Each member item an input supplied, in the order the configuration lists the members, then each item the workstream joined, by input in the configuration's order and then by id, each as its input reported it, less its notes. A joined item carries joined, so an item without it is a member. One item may join several workstreams, appearing once in each.

item.description: The item in supplied.v1's item shape, less notes, which lookout reads but never emits.

from.description: A workstream's name: for parent, the one holding the parent; for shared_item, whichever of the two comes first in stated order.

to.description: A workstream's name: for parent, the one holding the children; for shared_item, the other.

kind.description: shared_item, where both workstreams hold the same item; parent, where to holds an item whose parent, in the same input, from holds. A renderer should show a kind it does not know as a plain relation rather than drop it.

items.description: The items behind the link, as <input>:<id>, sorted: the shared items, or the children. Its length is the link's weight.

joined.description: Present on an item a workstream holds without naming it, saying why the workstream holds it.

by.description: How the item was matched to the member: key, where the key the item carries in a branch name or pull request title is the member's id; description, where a pull request's description names the member's id; notes, where a supplied item's notes name the member's id; pull_request, where the item is the branch, or a session on the branch, that an open pull request the workstream holds was made from, named in via; parent, where the member is the item's parent, or an ancestor reached through parents its input supplied, and is the nearest ancestor a live workstream names, the first such workstream in stated order. A renderer should show a value it does not know as a join rather than drop the item.

member.description: The member the item was matched to, as <input>:<id>: for pull_request, the member the pull request was matched to, or the pull request itself where it is a member; for parent, that ancestor, which the input need not have supplied.

via.description: The item this one joined through, as <input>:<id>; present where by is pull_request.

input.description: The awaiting input the entry came from.

workstreams.description: Every live workstream that names the subject as a member or holds it by a join, in stated order, whether or not the subject's input was read this time; empty where the entry has no subject or none holds it.

unplaced.description: Whether the subject is among the unplaced items. An entry whose subject is neither in a workstream nor unplaced concerns nothing the readout shows.
